levels.d: No evidence the outcome is addressed.
Documented, approved and applied across scope.
Measured, reviewed and enforced with evidence.
Continuously improved against metrics and threat change.

effort.M: Medium — project effort using existing tooling
effort.H: High — new capability, tooling or budget required

priority.d: More than 2.0 below the target maturity
At or above target — sustain the control

groups.name: ISMS requirements (clauses 4–10)
groups.desc: The management system requirements of ISO/IEC 27001:2022. These are mandatory for certification and cannot be excluded through the Statement of Applicability.

references.note: Indicative crosswalk to NIST CSF 2.0, provided so findings can be reported against either framework. It is not an accredited mapping — adjust the refs in this file where a customer needs it tuned. CSF outcomes with no ISO counterpart shown here are simply not referenced by any ISO control.

GV.OC-01.title: The organizational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management

GV.OC-02.title: Internal and external stakeholders are understood, and their needs and expectations regarding cybersecurity risk management are understood and considered

GV.OC-03.title: Legal, regulatory, and contractual requirements regarding cybersecurity - including privacy and civil liberties obligations - are understood and managed

GV.OC-04.title: Critical objectives, capabilities, and services that external stakeholders depend on or expect from the organization are understood and communicated

GV.OC-05.title: Outcomes, capabilities, and services that the organization depends on are understood and communicated

GV.RM-01.title: Risk management objectives are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders

GV.RM-02.title: Risk appetite and risk tolerance statements are established, communicated, and maintained

GV.RM-04.title: Strategic direction that describes appropriate risk response options is established and communicated

GV.RM-05.title: Lines of communication across the organization are established for cybersecurity risks, including risks from suppliers and other third parties

GV.RM-06.title: A standardized method for calculating, documenting, categorizing, and prioritizing cybersecurity risks is established and communicated

GV.RM-07.title: Strategic opportunities (i.e., positive risks) are characterized and are included in organizational cybersecurity risk discussions

GV.RR-01.title: Organizational leadership is responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk and fosters a culture that is risk-aware, ethical, and continually improving
GV.RR-01.meta: Govern · GV.RR · Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities

GV.RR-02.title: Roles, responsibilities, and authorities related to cybersecurity risk management are established, communicated, understood, and enforced
GV.RR-02.meta: Govern · GV.RR · Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities

GV.RR-03.title: Adequate resources are allocated commensurate with the cybersecurity risk strategy, roles, responsibilities, and policies
GV.RR-03.meta: Govern · GV.RR · Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities

GV.RR-04.title: Cybersecurity is included in human resources practices
GV.RR-04.meta: Govern · GV.RR · Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities

GV.PO-01.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is established based on organizational context, cybersecurity strategy, and priorities and is communicated and enforced

GV.PO-02.title: Policy for managing cybersecurity risks is reviewed, updated, communicated, and enforced to reflect changes in requirements, threats, technology, and organizational mission

GV.OV-01.title: Cybersecurity risk management strategy outcomes are reviewed to inform and adjust strategy and direction

GV.OV-02.title: The cybersecurity risk management strategy is reviewed and adjusted to ensure coverage of organizational requirements and risks

GV.OV-03.title: Organizational cybersecurity risk management performance is evaluated and reviewed for adjustments needed

GV.SC-01.title: A cybersecurity supply chain risk management program, strategy, objectives, policies, and processes are established and agreed to by organizational stakeholders
GV.SC-01.meta: Govern · GV.SC · Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management

GV.SC-02.title: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities for suppliers, customers, and partners are established, communicated, and coordinated internally and externally
GV.SC-02.meta: Govern · GV.SC · Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management

GV.SC-05.title: Requirements to address cybersecurity risks in supply chains are established, prioritized, and integrated into contracts and other types of agreements with suppliers and other relevant third parties
GV.SC-05.meta: Govern · GV.SC · Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management

GV.SC-06.title: Planning and due diligence are performed to reduce risks before entering into formal supplier or other third-party relationships
GV.SC-06.meta: Govern · GV.SC · Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management

GV.SC-07.title: The risks posed by a supplier, their products and services, and other third parties are understood, recorded, prioritized, assessed, responded to, and monitored over the course of the relationship
GV.SC-07.meta: Govern · GV.SC · Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management

GV.SC-10.title: Cybersecurity supply chain risk management plans include provisions for activities that occur after the conclusion of a partnership or service agreement
GV.SC-10.meta: Govern · GV.SC · Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management

ID.AM-01.title: Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained

ID.AM-02.title: Inventories of software, services, and systems managed by the organization are maintained

ID.AM-05.title: Assets are prioritized based on classification, criticality, resources, and impact on the mission

ID.AM-07.title: Inventories of data and corresponding metadata for designated data types are maintained

ID.AM-08.title: Systems, hardware, software, services, and data are managed throughout their life cycles

ID.RA-01.title: Vulnerabilities in assets are identified, validated, and recorded

ID.RA-02.title: Cyber threat intelligence is received from information sharing forums and sources

ID.RA-05.title: Threats, vulnerabilities, likelihoods, and impacts are used to understand inherent risk and inform risk response prioritization

ID.RA-06.title: Risk responses are chosen, prioritized, planned, tracked, and communicated

ID.RA-07.title: Changes and exceptions are managed, assessed for risk impact, recorded, and tracked

ID.RA-09.title: The authenticity and integrity of hardware and software are assessed prior to acquisition and use

ID.IM-02.title: Improvements are identified from security tests and exercises, including those done in coordination with suppliers and relevant third parties

ID.IM-03.title: Improvements are identified from execution of operational processes, procedures, and activities

ID.IM-04.title: Incident response plans and other cybersecurity plans that affect operations are established, communicated, maintained, and improved

PR.AA-01.title: Identities and credentials for authorized users, services, and hardware are managed by the organization
PR.AA-01.meta: Protect · PR.AA · Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

PR.AA-03.title: Users, services, and hardware are authenticated
PR.AA-03.meta: Protect · PR.AA · Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

PR.AA-05.title: Access permissions, entitlements, and authorizations are defined in a policy, managed, enforced, and reviewed, and incorporate the principles of least privilege and separation of duties
PR.AA-05.meta: Protect · PR.AA · Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

PR.AA-06.title: Physical access to assets is managed, monitored, and enforced commensurate with risk
PR.AA-06.meta: Protect · PR.AA · Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control

PR.AT-01.title: Personnel are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform general tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind

PR.AT-02.title: Individuals in specialized roles are provided with awareness and training so that they possess the knowledge and skills to perform relevant tasks with cybersecurity risks in mind

PR.DS-01.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-at-rest are protected

PR.DS-02.title: The confidentiality, integrity, and availability of data-in-transit are protected

PR.DS-11.title: Backups of data are created, protected, maintained, and tested

PR.PS-01.title: Configuration management practices are established and applied

PR.PS-02.title: Software is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

PR.PS-03.title: Hardware is maintained, replaced, and removed commensurate with risk

PR.PS-04.title: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring

PR.PS-05.title: Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented

PR.PS-06.title: Secure software development practices are integrated, and their performance is monitored throughout the software development life cycle

PR.IR-01.title: Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage

PR.IR-02.title: The organization's technology assets are protected from environmental threats

PR.IR-03.title: Mechanisms are implemented to achieve resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations

PR.IR-04.title: Adequate resource capacity to ensure availability is maintained

DE.CM-01.title: Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.CM-02.title: The physical environment is monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.CM-06.title: External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.CM-09.title: Computing hardware and software, runtime environments, and their data are monitored to find potentially adverse events

DE.AE-03.title: Information is correlated from multiple sources

DE.AE-07.title: Cyber threat intelligence and other contextual information are integrated into the analysis

DE.AE-08.title: Incidents are declared when adverse events meet the defined incident criteria

RS.MA-01.title: The incident response plan is executed in coordination with relevant third parties once an incident is declared

RS.MA-02.title: Incident reports are triaged and validated

RS.AN-03.title: Analysis is performed to establish what has taken place during an incident and the root cause of the incident

RS.AN-07.title: Incident data and metadata are collected, and their integrity and provenance are preserved

RS.CO-02.title: Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents
RS.CO-02.meta: Respond · RS.CO · Incident Response Reporting and Communication

RC.RP-01.title: The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated from the incident response process
RC.RP-01.meta: Recover · RC.RP · Incident Recovery Plan Execution

RC.RP-03.title: The integrity of backups and other restoration assets is verified before using them for restoration
RC.RP-03.meta: Recover · RC.RP · Incident Recovery Plan Execution

items.q: Are the external and internal issues relevant to the ISMS determined and kept current?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 4.1 — Understanding the organisation and its context
items.rec: Document the internal and external issues affecting the ISMS and review them at least annually and on material business change.

items.q: Are interested parties and their information security requirements, including legal and regulatory obligations, identified and maintained?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 4.2 — Needs and expectations of interested parties
items.rec: Maintain a register of interested parties and their requirements, distinguishing contractual, legal and regulatory obligations, with a named owner for each.

items.q: Is the ISMS scope documented, justified against the issues and interested parties, and available as documented information?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 4.3 — Determining the scope of the ISMS
items.rec: Publish a scope statement covering organisational units, locations, systems and interfaces, with documented justification for any exclusions.

items.q: Is the ISMS established, implemented, maintained and continually improved, including its processes and their interactions?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 4.4 — Information security management system
items.rec: Document the ISMS process model showing how the individual processes interact, and assign an owner to each.

items.q: Does top management demonstrate leadership and commitment by ensuring policy and objectives are set, resources provided, and the ISMS integrated into business processes?
items.rec: Evidence leadership commitment through documented resource decisions, objective setting and ISMS agenda items at an executive forum, not only through policy sign-off.

items.q: Is an information security policy established, appropriate to the organisation, approved by top management, communicated and available to interested parties?
items.rec: Maintain a top-management-approved information security policy that states the commitment to requirements and continual improvement, and evidence its communication.

items.q: Are ISMS roles, responsibilities and authorities assigned and communicated by top management?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 5.3 — Organisational roles, responsibilities and authorities
items.rec: Document ISMS roles and authorities including who reports ISMS performance to top management, and publish them beyond the security function.

items.q: Are risks and opportunities affecting ISMS outcomes determined and planned for?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 6.1.1 — Actions to address risks and opportunities
items.rec: Document how risks and opportunities to ISMS outcomes are determined, and how the actions taken are integrated into ISMS processes and evaluated for effectiveness.

items.q: Is a documented risk assessment process defined, including risk criteria, and applied consistently to produce comparable results?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 6.1.2 — Information security risk assessment
items.rec: Define and document risk acceptance and assessment criteria, identify risk owners, and ensure the method produces consistent, comparable and reproducible results.

items.q: Is a risk treatment process defined, with a Statement of Applicability, treatment plan and documented risk owner approval?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 6.1.3 — Information security risk treatment
items.rec: Maintain a Statement of Applicability covering all Annex A controls with inclusion or exclusion justification, and obtain documented risk-owner approval of the treatment plan and residual risk.

items.q: Are measurable security objectives established at relevant functions and levels, with plans stating what will be done, by whom and by when?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 6.2 — Information security objectives and planning
items.rec: Set measurable security objectives consistent with the policy, each with an owner, resource, deadline and method of evaluation.

items.q: Are changes to the ISMS carried out in a planned manner?
items.rec: Require ISMS changes — scope, policy, risk criteria, organisational structure — to be planned, assessed and approved rather than applied informally.

items.q: Are the resources needed for the ISMS determined and provided?
items.rec: Document the resources the ISMS requires and record any shortfall as an accepted risk where they cannot be provided.

items.q: Is the necessary competence determined, achieved and evidenced for people affecting information security performance?
items.rec: Define competence requirements per security role, assess against them, close gaps through training or recruitment, and retain evidence.

items.q: Are persons doing work under the organisation's control aware of the policy, their contribution and the implications of non-conformance?
items.rec: Ensure awareness activity covers the policy itself, individual contribution to the ISMS and the consequences of not conforming, and evidence coverage.

items.q: Are internal and external ISMS communications determined, including what, when, with whom and how?
items.rec: Document a communication plan covering what is communicated, to whom, when and by what means, for both routine and incident communication.

items.q: Is documented information created, updated and controlled, including version control, approval, distribution and protection?
items.rec: Operate document control covering identification, format, review and approval, availability, protection and retention, including externally originated documents.

items.q: Are the processes needed to meet security requirements planned, implemented and controlled, with outsourced processes controlled?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 8.1 — Operational planning and control
items.rec: Keep documented information sufficient to have confidence processes are carried out as planned, control changes and review unintended changes, and control outsourced processes.

items.q: Are risk assessments performed at planned intervals and when significant changes occur, with results retained?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 8.2 — Information security risk assessment (operation)
items.rec: Schedule risk assessments at defined intervals and trigger them on significant change, retaining documented results each time.

items.q: Is the risk treatment plan implemented, with results retained?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 8.3 — Information security risk treatment (operation)
items.rec: Track risk treatment plan implementation to completion with evidence retained for each treatment.

items.q: Is ISMS performance and effectiveness evaluated, with defined methods, timing and responsibility?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 9.1 — Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
items.rec: Define what is measured, by which method, when, by whom and when results are analysed, and retain the evidence as documented information.

items.q: Are internal audits conducted at planned intervals against an audit programme, by objective and impartial auditors?
items.rec: Operate a risk-based internal audit programme covering the whole ISMS over the certification cycle, with impartial auditors and results reported to management.

items.q: Does top management review the ISMS at planned intervals, covering the required inputs, with documented outputs?
items.rec: Hold management reviews covering all required inputs — prior actions, changes, performance, feedback, risk assessment results, improvement opportunities — and record decisions and actions.

items.q: Is the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the ISMS continually improved?
items.rec: Evidence continual improvement through a tracked improvement register fed by audits, incidents, reviews and operational experience.

items.q: Are nonconformities reacted to, root causes evaluated, corrective actions implemented and their effectiveness reviewed?
ex: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 clause 10.2 — Nonconformity and corrective action
items.rec: Maintain a nonconformity and corrective action log recording the nonconformity, correction, root cause analysis, action taken and effectiveness review.

items.q: Are information security policies defined, approved, published, communicated and reviewed at planned intervals or on significant change?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.1 — Policies for information security
items.rec: Maintain a topic-specific policy set beneath the overarching policy, each with an owner, approval record and review date, and evidence acknowledgement by staff.

items.q: Are information security roles and responsibilities defined and allocated according to organisational needs?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.2 — Information security roles and responsibilities
items.rec: Define and allocate security responsibilities including asset and risk ownership, and document them where the individuals concerned will see them.

items.q: Are conflicting duties and areas of responsibility segregated?
items.rec: Identify duties that must not be combined — such as requesting and approving privileged access — and enforce separation technically or through compensating review.

items.q: Does management require all personnel to apply information security in accordance with established policies and procedures?
items.rec: Make security expectations explicit in management objectives and line-manager briefings, so policy compliance is actively required rather than assumed.

items.q: Are appropriate contacts with relevant authorities established and maintained?
items.rec: Record named contacts and escalation routes for the national CSIRT, data protection authority, sector regulator and law enforcement, and verify them annually.

items.q: Are contacts with special interest groups, security forums and professional associations maintained?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.6 — Contact with special interest groups
items.rec: Maintain memberships or subscriptions that provide early warning and peer intelligence, and record how the input is used.

items.q: Is information relating to information security threats collected and analysed to produce threat intelligence?
items.rec: Formalise threat intelligence collection with named sources and owners, and document how strategic, tactical and operational intelligence changes controls.

items.q: Is information security integrated into project management?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.8 — Information security in project management
items.rec: Add security requirements, risk assessment and a security sign-off gate to the project lifecycle for all projects, not only IT projects.

items.q: Is an inventory of information and other associated assets, including owners, developed and maintained?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.9 — Inventory of information and other associated assets
items.rec: Maintain an asset inventory covering information as well as hardware and software, with a named owner for every entry and a documented reconciliation cycle.

items.q: Are rules for acceptable use of information and assets identified, documented and implemented?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.10 — Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
items.rec: Maintain an acceptable use policy covering corporate and personal devices, cloud services and removable media, and evidence acceptance by every user.

items.q: Are personnel and other interested parties required to return organisational assets on termination or change of employment?
items.rec: Include asset return in the leaver and role-change checklist with sign-off, covering devices, credentials, tokens and physical keys.

items.q: Is information classified according to confidentiality, integrity, availability and interested party requirements?
items.rec: Introduce a small classification scheme — typically three or four levels — with handling rules per level, and classify the highest-value information first.

items.q: Are procedures for information labelling developed and implemented in accordance with the classification scheme?
items.rec: Implement labelling in line with the classification scheme, using sensitivity labels in the productivity platform to make it automatic where possible.

items.q: Are information transfer rules, procedures and agreements in place for all types of transfer facility?
items.rec: Define transfer rules by classification level covering electronic, physical and verbal transfer, and put agreements in place with recipients of sensitive information.

items.q: Are rules to control physical and logical access to information and assets established and implemented based on business and security requirements?
items.rec: Maintain a documented access control policy applying least privilege and need-to-know, covering physical and logical access and reviewed on a fixed cycle.

items.q: Is the full lifecycle of identities managed?
items.rec: Manage the identity lifecycle from creation to removal for people, services and devices, with unique identities and no shared accounts.

items.q: Is the allocation and management of authentication information controlled by a management process?
items.rec: Control issue, distribution and revocation of authentication information, enforce strong authentication policy, and prohibit sharing of credentials.

items.q: Are access rights provisioned, reviewed, modified and removed in accordance with the access control policy?
items.rec: Operate a documented access review cycle covering privileged and business roles, and evidence removal of access no longer required.

items.q: Are processes and procedures defined to manage the security risks associated with the use of supplier products or services?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.19 — Information security in supplier relationships
items.rec: Establish a supplier security process covering identification, risk assessment and ongoing management, owned jointly by procurement and security.

items.q: Are relevant security requirements established and agreed with each supplier?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.20 — Addressing information security within supplier agreements
items.rec: Produce a standard contractual security schedule tiered by supplier criticality, covering obligations, incident notification, audit rights and subcontracting.

items.q: Are processes defined to manage the security risks associated with the ICT products and services supply chain?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.21 — Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
items.rec: Extend supplier assurance to the ICT supply chain including subcontractors and component provenance, and require suppliers to propagate requirements downstream.

items.q: Are changes to supplier services monitored, reviewed, evaluated and managed?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.22 — Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
items.rec: Schedule periodic supplier service reviews covering security performance, incidents and changes, with the frequency driven by supplier criticality.

items.q: Are processes for acquisition, use, management and exit from cloud services established in accordance with security requirements?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.23 — Information security for use of cloud services
items.rec: Define a cloud service lifecycle covering selection criteria, shared responsibility documentation, configuration standards, monitoring and a documented exit plan.

items.q: Is incident management planned and prepared, with roles and responsibilities defined?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.24 — Information security incident management planning and preparation
items.rec: Maintain an approved incident response plan with defined roles, severity criteria and escalation, and exercise it at least annually.

items.q: Are security events assessed and a decision made on whether they are to be categorised as incidents?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.25 — Assessment and decision on information security events
items.rec: Document event assessment and incident declaration criteria, and record the decision and the criteria met for each declared incident.

items.q: Are information security incidents responded to in accordance with documented procedures?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.26 — Response to information security incidents
items.rec: Develop incident type playbooks so response quality does not depend on who is available, and record actions taken against the plan.

items.q: Is knowledge gained from incidents used to strengthen and improve controls?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.27 — Learning from information security incidents
items.rec: Require a post-incident review producing root cause and tracked improvement actions for every incident above the defined severity threshold.

items.q: Are procedures established for the identification, collection, acquisition and preservation of evidence?
items.rec: Introduce an evidence handling procedure covering collection, hashing, storage and chain of custody, using a controlled repository rather than personal storage.

items.q: Is it planned how to maintain information security at an appropriate level during disruption?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.29 — Information security during disruption
items.rec: Document how security controls are maintained or compensated during disruption and failover, so degraded operation does not become insecure operation.

items.q: Is ICT readiness planned, implemented, maintained and tested based on business continuity objectives and ICT continuity requirements?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.30 — ICT readiness for business continuity
items.rec: Derive ICT recovery objectives from the business impact analysis and test them end to end at least annually.

items.q: Are legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements relevant to information security identified, documented and kept up to date?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.31 — Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
items.rec: Maintain a compliance obligations register with a named owner per obligation and a review triggered by regulatory change.

items.q: Are appropriate procedures implemented to protect intellectual property rights?
items.rec: Document IP and software licensing procedures, and reconcile licence entitlement against the software inventory periodically.

items.q: Are records protected from loss, destruction, falsification, unauthorised access and unauthorised release?
items.rec: Define retention and protection requirements per record type, and enforce them technically through retention policy and access control.

items.q: Are requirements for privacy and PII protection identified and met in accordance with applicable law and regulation?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.34 — Privacy and protection of personally identifiable information
items.rec: Maintain records of processing, DPIA triggers and data subject rights procedures, and align technical controls to the PII inventory.

items.q: Is the approach to managing information security independently reviewed at planned intervals or on significant change?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.35 — Independent review of information security
items.rec: Schedule independent review of the security approach — internal audit, second line or external assessment — at a defined interval.

items.q: Is compliance with the security policy, topic-specific policies, rules and standards regularly reviewed?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 5.36 — Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
items.rec: Introduce periodic compliance checking against policies and standards, with results reported to the owner and nonconformities tracked.

items.q: Are operating procedures for information processing facilities documented and made available?
items.rec: Document operating procedures for the activities that would be hard to perform correctly from memory, and keep them accessible during a disruption.

items.q: Are background verification checks on candidates carried out prior to joining and proportionate to the role?
items.rec: Apply proportionate pre-employment screening to employees and contractors before access is granted, and retain evidence of completion.

items.q: Do employment contractual agreements state the personnel's and the organisation's responsibilities for information security?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 6.2 — Terms and conditions of employment
items.rec: Ensure contracts of employment and contractor agreements state security responsibilities, including those continuing after termination.

items.q: Do personnel receive appropriate awareness, education and training, and regular updates, relevant to their job function?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 6.3 — Information security awareness, education and training
items.rec: Deliver induction and annual refresher awareness to all personnel, with role-relevant content and completion tracked.

items.q: Is a disciplinary process formalised and communicated for personnel who have committed a security policy violation?
items.rec: Document and communicate the disciplinary process for security violations so that policy enforcement is credible.

items.q: Are security responsibilities that remain valid after termination or change of employment defined, enforced and communicated?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 6.5 — Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
items.rec: Define and communicate continuing obligations at exit, and enforce timely revocation of all access on termination or role change.

items.q: Are confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements identified, documented, regularly reviewed and signed?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 6.6 — Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
items.rec: Maintain reviewed NDA templates for personnel and third parties, and track signature and renewal.

items.q: Are security measures implemented when personnel work remotely to protect information accessed, processed or stored outside the premises?
items.rec: Maintain a remote working standard covering device compliance, VPN or zero-trust access, physical precautions and home network guidance.

items.q: Is a mechanism provided for personnel to report observed or suspected security events in a timely manner?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 6.8 — Information security event reporting
items.rec: Provide a simple, well-publicised reporting route with a target response time, and give reporters feedback so the behaviour is reinforced.

items.q: Are security perimeters defined and used to protect areas containing information and other associated assets?
items.rec: Define physical security perimeters around areas holding sensitive information or critical equipment, documented on a site plan.

items.q: Are secure areas protected by appropriate entry controls and access points?
items.rec: Enforce individual credential access to secure areas with separate authorisation groups, logging, and consistent visitor escort and recording.

items.q: Is physical security for offices, rooms and facilities designed and implemented?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 7.3 — Securing offices, rooms and facilities
items.rec: Apply physical protection proportionate to the sensitivity of each area, including lockable storage for sensitive material.

items.q: Are premises continuously monitored for unauthorised physical access?
items.rec: Maintain physical monitoring such as CCTV and intruder detection with defined retention, and route alerts to a party that will act on them.

items.q: Is protection against physical and environmental threats such as fire, flood and other natural or intentional threats designed and implemented?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 7.5 — Protecting against physical and environmental threats
items.rec: Assess environmental threats per site and implement detection and protection accordingly, with alerting rather than passive equipment alone.

items.q: Are security measures for working in secure areas designed and implemented?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 7.6 — Working in secure areas
items.rec: Document rules for working in secure areas, including restrictions on recording devices and unsupervised working.

items.q: Are clear desk rules for papers and removable media and clear screen rules defined and enforced?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 7.7 — Clear desk and clear screen
items.rec: Enforce clear screen technically through automatic session locking, and reinforce clear desk expectations through awareness and spot checks.

items.q: Is equipment sited securely and protected?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 7.8 — Equipment siting and protection
items.rec: Site equipment to reduce environmental risk and unauthorised viewing, and secure equipment in shared or public-facing areas.

items.q: Are off-site assets protected?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 7.9 — Security of assets off-premises
items.rec: Apply encryption, tracking and remote wipe to off-site assets, and document handling rules for equipment taken off premises.

items.q: Is storage media managed through its lifecycle of acquisition, use, transportation and disposal?
items.rec: Manage removable and fixed media through its lifecycle with encryption in use and transport, and certified destruction at disposal.

items.q: Are information processing facilities protected from power failures and other disruptions caused by failures in supporting utilities?
items.rec: Maintain and test UPS and other supporting utilities, and replace units past end-of-support before they fail.

items.q: Are cables carrying power, data or supporting information services protected from interception, interference or damage?
items.rec: Protect and label cabling, segregate power from data, and secure patching areas against unauthorised access.

items.q: Is equipment maintained correctly to ensure availability, integrity and confidentiality of information?
items.rec: Maintain equipment to vendor schedules by authorised personnel, and record maintenance including any off-site repair of media-bearing equipment.

items.q: Are items of equipment containing storage media verified to ensure sensitive data and licensed software are removed or securely overwritten prior to disposal or re-use?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 7.14 — Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
items.rec: Use certified data destruction with retained certificates for all media-bearing equipment at disposal or re-use.

items.q: Is information stored on, processed by or accessible via user endpoint devices protected?
items.rec: Manage all endpoints through a device management platform enforcing encryption, patching, screen lock, malware protection and remote wipe.

items.q: Is the allocation and use of privileged access rights restricted and managed?
items.rec: Restrict privileged access to dedicated administrative accounts, keep the standing privileged population minimal, and review privileged entitlements on a defined cycle.

items.q: Is access to information and other associated assets restricted in accordance with the established access control policy?
items.rec: Apply least-privilege access restriction driven by information classification, and review effective permissions on sensitive repositories.

items.q: Is read and write access to source code, development tools and software libraries appropriately managed?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.4 — Access to source code
items.rec: Control access to source repositories and pipelines with least privilege, branch protection and audit logging, including low-code platform environments.

items.q: Are secure authentication technologies and procedures implemented based on information access restrictions and the access control policy?
items.rec: Enforce multi-factor authentication for remote, administrative and cloud access, eliminating legacy authentication paths.

items.q: Is the use of resources monitored and adjusted in line with current and expected capacity requirements?
items.rec: Monitor capacity against defined thresholds with alerting, and maintain a documented forward capacity forecast.

items.q: Is protection against malware implemented and supported by appropriate user awareness?
items.rec: Maintain centrally managed anti-malware with current signatures across the estate, supported by awareness training and email and web filtering.

items.q: Is information about technical vulnerabilities obtained, exposure evaluated and appropriate measures taken?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.8 — Management of technical vulnerabilities
items.rec: Operate authenticated vulnerability scanning across the estate with risk-based prioritisation and remediation tracked to closure against defined SLAs.

items.q: Are configurations, including security configurations, of hardware, software, services and networks established, documented, implemented, monitored and reviewed?
items.rec: Define configuration baselines from a recognised benchmark, apply them to every system, and monitor for drift rather than relying on build-time compliance.

items.q: Is information stored in information systems, devices or other storage media deleted when no longer required?
items.rec: Apply retention schedules technically through retention policies and automated deletion, covering cloud collaboration data as well as structured systems.

items.q: Is data masking used in accordance with the topic-specific policy on access control and business requirements, taking applicable legislation into consideration?
items.rec: Mask or pseudonymise sensitive data where full values are not needed, particularly in test environments and reporting.

items.q: Are data leakage prevention measures applied to systems, networks and devices that process, store or transmit sensitive information?
items.rec: Deploy data loss prevention on the highest-risk channels — email, cloud storage and removable media — starting in monitor mode to baseline before enforcement.

items.q: Are backup copies of information, software and systems maintained and regularly tested in accordance with the agreed backup policy?
items.rec: Maintain backups to a documented standard with immutability and offsite copy, and restore-test on schedule including at least one full system recovery per year.

items.q: Are information processing facilities implemented with redundancy sufficient to meet availability requirements?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.14 — Redundancy of information processing facilities
items.rec: Provide redundancy proportionate to the availability requirement and test failover end to end so the stated objectives are evidenced.

items.q: Are logs recording activities, exceptions, faults and other relevant events produced, stored, protected and analysed?
items.rec: Generate logs on all in-scope systems to a defined standard, protect them from modification, and retain them for the documented period.

items.q: Are networks, systems and applications monitored for anomalous behaviour and appropriate actions taken to evaluate potential incidents?
items.rec: Deploy central log aggregation and correlation covering identity, endpoint, network and cloud, with defined use cases and named review ownership.

items.q: Are the clocks of information processing systems synchronised to approved time sources?
items.rec: Synchronise all systems to authoritative time sources so that log timestamps are reliable for correlation and evidence.

items.q: Is the use of utility programs capable of overriding system and application controls restricted and tightly controlled?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.18 — Use of privileged utility programs
items.rec: Restrict and log the use of privileged utilities, removing them where not required and controlling access where they are.

items.q: Are procedures and measures implemented to securely manage software installation on operational systems?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.19 — Installation of software on operational systems
items.rec: Prevent unauthorised software installation through non-administrative user rights and application control, with a documented approval route for exceptions.

items.q: Are networks and network devices secured, managed and controlled to protect information in systems and applications?
items.rec: Secure network devices with hardened configuration, authenticated encrypted management, documented rulesets and change control.

items.q: Are security mechanisms, service levels and service requirements of network services identified, implemented and monitored?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.21 — Security of network services
items.rec: Document the security requirements and service levels for each network service, including third-party circuits, and monitor delivery against them.

items.q: Are groups of information services, users and information systems segregated in the organisation's networks?
items.rec: Segment networks by trust level and function, and restrict east-west traffic within segments to constrain lateral movement.

items.q: Is access to external websites managed to reduce exposure to malicious content?
items.rec: Enforce DNS and URL filtering for all users including remote workers, with bypass prevented at the perimeter.

items.q: Are rules for the effective use of cryptography, including cryptographic key management, defined and implemented?
items.rec: Maintain a cryptography standard covering approved algorithms, protocol versions and full key lifecycle management including escrow and rotation.

items.q: Are rules for the secure development of software and systems established and applied?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.25 — Secure development life cycle
items.rec: Define a secure development lifecycle proportionate to what the organisation actually builds, explicitly including low-code and citizen development.

items.q: Are information security requirements identified, specified and approved when developing or acquiring applications?
items.rec: Require security requirements to be specified and approved for every application developed or acquired, covering authentication, authorisation and data protection.

items.q: Are principles for engineering secure systems established, documented, maintained and applied?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.27 — Secure system architecture and engineering principles
items.rec: Document secure architecture principles — defence in depth, least privilege, secure defaults, fail secure — and apply them as design review criteria.

items.q: Are secure coding principles applied to software development?
items.rec: Adopt a secure coding standard with developer training and code review, extending to anyone building automations on low-code platforms.

items.q: Are security testing processes defined and implemented in the development life cycle?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.29 — Security testing in development and acceptance
items.rec: Define security testing gates in development and acceptance, and require testing evidence before production release.

items.q: Is outsourced system development directed, monitored and reviewed?
items.rec: Set security requirements, evidence expectations and right-to-test in outsourced development contracts, and verify delivery against them.

items.q: Are development, testing and production environments separated and secured?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.31 — Separation of development, test and production environments
items.rec: Separate development, test and production environments technically and by access, including low-code platform environments currently built in production.

items.q: Are changes to information processing facilities and information systems subject to change management procedures?
items.rec: Apply change control with risk assessment, approval, testing and rollback to all environments, including emergency changes documented retrospectively within a defined window.

items.q: Is test information appropriately selected, protected and managed?
items.rec: Prohibit unmasked production data in test environments, using synthetic or masked data with documented approval for any exception.

items.q: Are audit tests and other assurance activities involving assessment of operational systems planned and agreed between the tester and appropriate management?
ex: ISO/IEC 27002:2022 control 8.34 — Protection of information systems during audit testing
items.rec: Agree scope, timing, access and rules of engagement for audit and penetration testing in advance, with read-only access wherever practicable.
